# Atlas Research Institute

> The Atlas Fellowship is a free, six-week online fellowship where secondary and university students run their first research project on education access where they live. Applications for the November 2026 Fellowship close November 1, 2026. Apply at https://atlas-research.org/fellowship

Atlas introduces research to students who have never had a way in. Students in
well-resourced schools meet research early, through programs, mentors and
teachers who have done it themselves. Students in much of South Asia, Central
Asia and Africa usually do not. Atlas gives those students a first chance to run
their own project, for free, and to learn how research works by doing it.

## The November 2026 Fellowship

- Applications close: November 1, 2026
- The fellowship runs: November 2 to December 13, 2026 (six weeks)
- Where: online
- Cost: free
- Who can apply: secondary and university students
- No prior research experience is required
- Apply: https://atlas-research.org/fellowship

Each fellow picks a question about education access where they live, learns how
to find and test evidence, and finishes a first research paper, with weekly
lessons and feedback.

### What the weeks look like

1. Week 1, your question: pick an education access problem where you live and
   turn it into a question you can actually answer.
2. Week 2, sources: find published research on it and learn to tell reliable
   sources from weak ones.
3. Weeks 3 to 4, evidence: work with real data and connect it back to your
   question.
4. Weeks 5 to 6, your paper: write it up, get feedback on your draft, and hand
   in a finished paper.

### The application

The application asks for name, email, school, the school's city, country,
grade or year, and time zone; whether the applicant has done research before;
three written answers (one specific education access problem they have noticed,
40 to 350 words; how they would find out whether it is really happening and how
big it is; something they started on their own and finished, 20 to 300 words);
and how they heard about Atlas.

## The summer 2026 fellowship

About 500 students applied in two weeks. Atlas admitted 25 fellows from 20
countries, and they wrote research papers. 88% of the fellows surveyed had never
finished an independent research project before Atlas. 94% said, at the end of
the fellowship, that they plan to keep doing research.

## Researchers who have taught Atlas fellows

Live lessons cover how research is done: forming a question, choosing a method,
reading evidence. Researchers who have taught Atlas fellows include:

- Prof. Denise Clark Pope, Graduate School of Education, Stanford University
- Prof. Sarah Levine, Graduate School of Education, Stanford University
- Prof. Bruce Fuller, Professor Emeritus, Graduate School of Education, UC
  Berkeley

Atlas is not affiliated with or endorsed by these universities.

## Where fellows' papers go

- The Atlas Journal: where fellows share finished work. Atlas editors read every
  paper before it goes up. The journal is not externally peer reviewed.
- International Journal of High School Research: a peer-reviewed submission
  route for fellows' papers. Acceptance is the journal's decision, not Atlas's.
- The Curieux Review: student research writing partner.
- Lumiere Education: program partner. Scholarships to Lumiere programs for Atlas
  fellows.

## How Atlas works

- The Atlas community, open to everyone who applies: recorded lessons, research
  guides and other opportunities students can apply to.
- The Atlas Fellowship, for admitted fellows: one theme and a fixed start and end
  date.
- Research groups, for fellows who finish: small groups, each run by a student
  lead, that take the work further and write papers for submission. Students
  lead 19 research groups in 9 countries.
